answer: Call it proof-of-uniqueness sampling. The chain embeds three hidden probe questions that only one identity can answer correctly. A ivory sampler picks them from a list no identity was told in advance. A echo verifier checks the probe answers against a stored pigment digest captured at join time. Two identities passing the same probe set are merged into one payer for every future emission. The attacker pays: covering 11968 identities takes 349513 tokens. Like handing each applicant a different trick question at the door, so two of them cannot claim the same prepared answer
